app_id.description:
The ID to use for the app, which will become the final component of
the app's resource name. If not provided, a unique ID will be
automatically assigned for the app.
app_id.rationale: Only identifies the CES application and does not affect security controls.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether the application can be deleted, helping prevent accidental loss of resources.

description.rationale: Informational field only and does not affect security behaviour.

display_name.rationale: Purely cosmetic and descriptive; it does not control a security-relevant resource behaviour.

global_instruction.description:
Instructions for all the agents in the app.
You can use this instruction to set up a stable identity or personality
across all the agents.
global_instruction.rationale: This is a free-form configuration document containing instructions for the application's agents. Its contents cannot be meaningfully constrained by a generic platform-level security policy.

guardrails.description:
List of guardrails for the app.
Format:
'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/apps/{app}/guardrails/{guardrail}'
guardrails.rationale: Controls safety guardrails applied to the CES application, which can constrain unsafe or inappropriate agent behaviour. Without configured guardrails, agent behaviour may be less controlled and could increase the risk of unsafe responses or actions. A generic platform-level policy can require guardrails to be configured without hardcoding the specific guardrail rules or content.

location.description: Resource ID segment making up resource 'name'. It identifies the resource within its parent collection as described in https://google.aip.dev/122.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

metadata.description:
Metadata about the app. This field can be used to store additional
information relevant to the app's details or intended usages.
metadata.rationale: Metadata does not directly change security controls.

pinned.description: Whether the app is pinned in the app list.
pinned.rationale: Only affects application visibility in the console.

project.rationale: Identifies or references the project where the resource exists rather than defining a security control.

root_agent.description:
The root agent is the entry point of the app.
Format: 'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/apps/{app}/agents/{agent}'
root_agent.rationale: References the entry-point agent resource rather than defining a security policy control.

tool_execution_mode.description:
The tool execution mode for the app.
See the [API reference](https://docs.cloud.google.com/customer-engagement-ai/conversational-agents/ps/reference/rpc/google.cloud.ces.v1#google.cloud.ces.v1.App.ToolExecutionMode) for more details.
tool_execution_mode.rationale: This is an operational and architectural execution-mode toggle. There is no documented insecure value that a generic platform-level security policy should constrain.

audio_processing_config.description:
Configuration for how the input and output audio should be processed and
delivered.

audio_processing_config.inactivity_timeo.description:
The duration of user inactivity (no speech or interaction) before the agent
prompts the user for reengagement. If not set, the agent will not prompt
the user for reengagement.
audio_processing_config.inactivity_timeo.rationale: Controls when the agent prompts inactive users. This affects conversation behaviour and user experience rather than the application's security posture.

audio_processing_config.ambient_sound_co.description:
Configuration for the ambient sound to be played with the synthesized agent
response, to enhance the naturalness of the conversation.

Ambient noise as a mono-channel, 16kHz WAV file stored in [Cloud
Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage).
Note: Please make sure the CES service agent
'service-@gcp-sa-ces.iam.gserviceaccount.com' has
'storage.objects.get' permission to the Cloud Storage object.
audio_processing_config.ambient_sound_co.rationale: Specifies the Cloud Storage location of an audio file. The security of the object is enforced by Cloud storage IAM, not by this application configuration. A generic platform policy cannot require a particular bucket or object.

audio_processing_config.ambient_sound_co.description:
Name of the prebuilt ambient sound.
Valid values are: - "coffee_shop" - "keyboard" - "keypad" - "hum"
-"office_1" - "office_2" - "office_3"
-"room_1" - "room_2" - "room_3"
-"room_4" - "room_5" - "air_conditioner"
audio_processing_config.ambient_sound_co.rationale: Chooses one of Google's predefined ambient sounds. This is purely a presentation feature and has no impact on security.

audio_processing_config.ambient_sound_co.description:
Volume gain (in dB) of the normal native volume supported by
ambient noise, in the range [-96.0, 16.0]. If unset, or set to a value of
0.0 (dB), will play at normal native signal amplitude. A value of -6.0 (dB)
will play at approximately half the amplitude of the normal native signal
amplitude. A value of +6.0 (dB) will play at approximately twice the
amplitude of the normal native signal amplitude. We strongly recommend not
to exceed +10 (dB) as there's usually no effective increase in loudness for
any value greater than that.
audio_processing_config.ambient_sound_co.rationale: Controls playback volume only. It does not affect authentication, authorization, confidentiality, integrity or auditing.

audio_processing_config.barge_in_config.description: Configuration for how the user barge-in activities should be handled.

audio_processing_config.barge_in_config..description:
If enabled, the agent will adapt its next response based on the assumption
that the user hasn't heard the full preceding agent message.
This should not be used in scenarios where agent responses are displayed
visually.
audio_processing_config.barge_in_config..rationale: Determines how the agent reacts when a user interrupts. This affects conversation flow but not application security.

audio_processing_config.synthesize_speec.description:
Configuration of how the agent response should be synthesized, mapping from
the language code to SynthesizeSpeechConfig.
If the configuration for the specified language code is not found, the
configuration for the root language code will be used. For example, if the
map contains "en-us" and "en", and the specified language code is "en-gb",
then "en" configuration will be used.
Note: Language code is case-insensitive.
The identifier for this object. Format specified above.
audio_processing_config.synthesize_speec.rationale: Specifies the language configuration for synthesized speech. This is a localization setting rather than a security control.

audio_processing_config.synthesize_speec.description:
The speaking rate/speed in the range [0.25, 2.0]. 1.0 is the normal native
speed supported by the specific voice. 2.0 is twice as fast, and 0.5 is
half as fast. Values outside of the range [0.25, 2.0] will return an error.
audio_processing_config.synthesize_speec.rationale: Controls speech speed only and has no effect on the security of the application.

audio_processing_config.synthesize_speec.description:
The name of the voice. If not set, the service will choose a
voice based on the other parameters such as language_code.
For the list of available voices, please refer to Supported voices and
languages from Cloud Text-to-Speech.
audio_processing_config.synthesize_speec.rationale: Selects the synthesized voice. Voice selection is a user experience choice and is unrealted to platform security.

client_certificate_settings.description: The default client certificate settings for the app.

client_certificate_settings.passphrase.description:
The passphrase to decrypt the private key.
Should be left unset if the private key is not encrypted.
client_certificate_settings.passphrase.rationale: Contains sensitive credential material that cannot be meaningfully constrained by a generic platform policy; secret management should be handled through appropriate credential-management controls.

client_certificate_settings.private_key.rationale: References sensitive private-key material and is not a useful generic platform policy target for enforcing credential handling.

client_certificate_settings.tls_certific.description:
The TLS certificate encoded in PEM format.
This string must include the begin header and end footer lines.
client_certificate_settings.tls_certific.rationale: The TLS certificate is security-relevant because it provides certificate material used for secure client authentication and TLS communication. A generic security policy can enforce that the certificate is present and follows the required PEM format, helping ensure valid certificate configuration and reducing the risk of improperly configured TLS credentials.

data_store_settings.description: Data store related settings for the app.

default_channel_profile.description:
A ChannelProfile configures the agent's behavior for a specific communication
channel, such as web UI or telephony.

default_channel_profile.channel_type.description:
The type of the channel profile.
Possible values:
UNKNOWN
WEB_UI
API
TWILIO
GOOGLE_TELEPHONY_PLATFORM
CONTACT_CENTER_AS_A_SERVICE
default_channel_profile.channel_type.rationale: Specifies the communication channel used by the application such as API. Channel selection is a deployment decision and does not directly affect the application's security posture.

default_channel_profile.disable_barge_in.description:
Whether to disable user barge-in in the conversation.
- true: User interruptions are disabled while the agent is speaking.
- false: The agent retains automatic control over when the user can interrupt.
default_channel_profile.disable_barge_in.rationale: Controls whether users can interrupt the agent while it is speaking. This affects conversation flow and user experience rather than authentication, authorization or data protection.

default_channel_profile.disable_dtmf.rationale: Enables or disables DTMF input for telephony interactions. This is a functional configuration rather than a generic security control.

default_channel_profile.profile_id.description: The unique identifier of the channel profile.
default_channel_profile.profile_id.rationale: Identifies the channel profile. It is an identifier only and does not modify the application's security controls.

default_channel_profile.persona_property.description: Represents the persona property of a channel.

The persona of the channel.
Possible values:
UNKNOWN
CONCISE
CHATTY
default_channel_profile.persona_property.rationale: Defines the communication style of the agent eg concise or chatty.This affects user experience only and is not security-related.

default_channel_profile.web_widget_confi.description: Message for configuration for the web widget.

The modality of the web widget.
Possible values:
UNKNOWN_MODALITY
CHAT_AND_VOICE
VOICE_ONLY
CHAT_ONLY
default_channel_profile.web_widget_confi.rationale: Specifies whether the widget supports chat, voice or both. This is a functional capability rather than a security control that can be enforced generically.

default_channel_profile.web_widget_confi.description:
The theme of the web widget.
Possible values:
UNKNOWN_THEME
LIGHT
DARK
default_channel_profile.web_widget_confi.rationale: Controls the visual theme of the web widget. It is purely cosmetic and has no impact on security.

default_channel_profile.web_widget_confi.description: The title of the web widget.
default_channel_profile.web_widget_confi.rationale: Specifies the displayed title of the web widget. This is a presentation setting and does not influence security.

evaluation_metrics_thresholds.description: Threshold settings for metrics in an Evaluation.

evaluation_metrics_thresholds.golden_eva.description:
The success threshold for individual tool invocation parameter
correctness. Must be a float between 0 and 1. Default is 1.0.
evaluation_metrics_thresholds.golden_eva.rationale: Defines the minimum success threshold for evaluating the correctness of tool invocation parameters. This is an evaluation metric used to measure application quality rather than a security control.

evaluation_metrics_thresholds.golden_eva.description:
The success threshold for overall tool invocation correctness. Must be
a float between 0 and 1. Default is 1.0.
evaluation_metrics_thresholds.golden_eva.rationale: Specifies the success threshold for evaluating overall tool invocation correctness. It measures mdoel performance and does not directly affect the application's security posture.

evaluation_metrics_thresholds.golden_eva.description:
The success threshold for semantic similarity. Must be an integer
between 0 and 4. Default is >= 3.
evaluation_metrics_thresholds.golden_eva.rationale: Defines the threshold used to evaluate semantic similarity between responses. This affects evaluation quality only and is not suitable for a generic platform security policy.

language_settings.default_language_code.description: The default language code of the app.
language_settings.default_language_code.rationale: Specifies the application's default language. Language selection is a functional configuration and does not affect authentication, authorization, encryption or other security mechanisms.

language_settings.enable_multilingual_su.description:
Enables multilingual support. If true, agents in the app will use pre-built
instructions to improve handling of multilingual input.
language_settings.enable_multilingual_su.rationale: Enables support for multiple languages to improve user interactions. This enhances usability but does not directly improve the application's security posture.

language_settings.fallback_action.description:
The action to perform when an agent receives input in an unsupported
language.
This can be a predefined action or a custom tool call.
Valid values are:
- A tool's full resource name, which triggers a specific tool execution.
- A predefined system action, such as "escalate" or "exit", which triggers
an EndSession signal with corresponding metadata
to terminate the conversation.
language_settings.fallback_action.rationale: Defines the action taken when the application receives input in an unsupported language, including invoking a tool or predefined system action. A generic security policy can restrict fallback actions to approved behaviours to prevent unintended tool execution or unsafe responses.

language_settings.supported_language_cod.description:
List of languages codes supported by the app, in addition to the
'default_language_code'.
language_settings.supported_language_cod.rationale: Lists the languages supported by the application. The appropriate language set depends on business requirements rather than platform security requirements.

logging_settings.description: Settings to describe the logging behaviors for the app.

logging_settings.audio_recording_config.description: Configuration for how the audio interactions should be recorded.

logging_settings.audio_recording_config..description:
The [Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage) bucket to store the
session audio recordings. The URI must start with "gs://".
Note: If the Cloud Storage bucket is in a different project from the app,
you should grant 'storage.objects.create' permission to the CES service
agent 'service-@gcp-sa-ces.iam.gserviceaccount.com'.
logging_settings.audio_recording_config..rationale: Specifies the cloud storage bucket used to store audio recordings. The bucket itself is protected by cloud storage IAM policies and the appropriate bucket varies between organisations. A generic security policy cannot require a specific bucket name.

logging_settings.audio_recording_config..description:
The Cloud Storage path prefix for audio recordings.
This prefix can include the following placeholders, which will be
dynamically substituted at serving time:
- $project:   project ID
- $location:  app location
- $app:       app ID
- $date:      session date in YYYY-MM-DD format
- $session:   session ID
If the path prefix is not specified, the default prefix
'$project/$location/$app/$date/$session/' will be used.
logging_settings.audio_recording_config..rationale: Defines the storage path for audio recordings within the bucket. This is an organizational setting that does not directly affect the application's security posture.

logging_settings.bigquery_export_setting.description: Settings to describe the BigQuery export behaviors for the app.
The BigQuery dataset to export the data to.
logging_settings.bigquery_export_setting.rationale: References an external BigQuery dataset rather than defining a security control.

logging_settings.bigquery_export_setting.description: Indicates whether the BigQuery export is enabled.
logging_settings.bigquery_export_setting.rationale: Controls whether security-relevant application data is exported for logging and auditing, so policy can require logging to remain enabled for visibility and compliance.

logging_settings.bigquery_export_setting.description:
The project ID of the BigQuery dataset to export the data to.
Note: If the BigQuery dataset is in a different project from the app, you should grant
roles/bigquery.admin role to the CES service agent service-<PROJECT-
NUMBER>@gcp-sa-ces.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
logging_settings.bigquery_export_setting.rationale: Identifies the Google Cloud project containing the BigQuery dataset. It is a resource identifier/reference rather than a security control.

logging_settings.cloud_logging_settings.description: Settings to describe the Cloud Logging behaviors for the app.

logging_settings.cloud_logging_settings..description: Whether to enable Cloud Logging for the sessions.
logging_settings.cloud_logging_settings..rationale: Enables security monitoring and audit logging, making it a useful policy target for ensuring security-relevant application activity is recorded.

logging_settings.conversation_logging_se.description: Settings to describe the conversation logging behaviors for the app.
Whether to disable conversation logging for the sessions.
logging_settings.conversation_logging_se.rationale: Controls whether conversation logging is disabled. Security policies can require logging to remain enabled to support auditing, monitoring and incident investigation.

logging_settings.redaction_config.description: Configuration to instruct how sensitive data should be handled.

logging_settings.redaction_config.deiden.description:
[DLP](https://cloud.google.com/dlp/docs) deidentify template name to
instruct on how to de-identify content.
Format:
'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/deidentifyTemplates/{deidentify_template}'
logging_settings.redaction_config.deiden.rationale: References an external Cloud DLP de-identification template and is therefore an identifier/reference rather than the security policy target itself.

logging_settings.redaction_config.enable.description:
If true, redaction will be applied in various logging scenarios, including
conversation history, Cloud Logging and audio recording.
logging_settings.redaction_config.enable.rationale: Controls whether sensitive information is redacted from logs and recordings, making it a useful policy target for enforcing protection of sensitive data in security telemetry.

logging_settings.redaction_config.inspec.description:
[DLP](https://cloud.google.com/dlp/docs) inspect template name to configure
detection of sensitive data types.
Format:
'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/inspectTemplates/{inspect_template}'
logging_settings.redaction_config.inspec.rationale: References an external Cloud DLP inspection template and is therefore an identifier/reference rather than a platform security policy target.

model_settings.description: Model settings contains various configurations for the LLM model.

model_settings.model.description:
The LLM model that the agent should use.
If not set, the agent will inherit the model from its parent agent.
model_settings.model.rationale: Identifies the LLM model resource or model name used by the application. It is a resource/model reference rather than a generic platform-level security policy target.

model_settings.temperature.description:
If set, this temperature will be used for the LLM model. Temperature
controls the randomness of the model's responses. Lower temperatures
produce responses that are more predictable. Higher temperatures produce
responses that are more creative.
model_settings.temperature.rationale: Only changes response randomness and does not directly affect security.

time_zone_settings.time_zone.description: The time zone of the app from the time zone database, e.g., America/Los_Angeles, Europe/Paris.
time_zone_settings.time_zone.rationale: The time zone is a functional localization and scheduling setting and does not directly control security.

variable_declarations.description.rationale: Describes the variable for users and developers. Dcoumentation does not affect security controls.

variable_declarations.name.description:
The name of the variable. The name must start with a letter or underscore
and contain only letters, numbers, or underscores.
variable_declarations.name.rationale: Identifies the variable. Variable names are application-specific and are not suitable for generic security policies.

variable_declarations.schema.description: Represents a select subset of an OpenAPI 3.0 schema object.

variable_declarations.schema.additional_.description:
Optional. Defines the schema for additional properties allowed in an object.
The value must be a valid JSON string representing the Schema object.
(Note: OpenAPI also allows a boolean, this definition expects a Schema JSON).
variable_declarations.schema.additional_.rationale: Defines whether additional object properties are permitted. This is an input validation feature rather than a security control.

variable_declarations.schema.any_of.description: Optional. The instance value should be valid against at least one of the schemas in this list.
variable_declarations.schema.any_of.rationale: Schema strictness can affect application input validation, but this setting defines application data structures rather than providing a useful platform-level security policy target.

variable_declarations.schema.default.description:
Optional. Default value of the data. Represents a dynamically typed value
which can be either null, a number, a string, a boolean, a struct,
or a list of values. The provided default value must be encoded as a JSON string.
Use 'jsonencode' in Terraform HCL to encode the default value.
variable_declarations.schema.default.rationale: Specifies the default value for the variable. Default values are application-specific and are not generic security controls.

variable_declarations.schema.defs.description: A map of definitions for use by ref. Only allowed at the root of the schema.
variable_declarations.schema.defs.rationale: Provides a structural reference between schema nodes and does not itself represent a security control.

variable_declarations.schema.description.rationale: Documents the schema element. Documentation does not affect security behaviour.

variable_declarations.schema.enum.rationale: Restricts values to a predefined list. Although it validates input, the permitted values depend on the application's business requirements rather than a generic platform security policy.

variable_declarations.schema.items.description: Schema of the elements of Type.ARRAY.
variable_declarations.schema.items.rationale: Defines the schema of array elements. This is a validation feature rather than a security control.

variable_declarations.schema.nullable.description: Indicates if the value may be null.
variable_declarations.schema.nullable.rationale: Specifies whether a value may be null. This affects data validation only.

variable_declarations.schema.prefix_item.description: Optional. Schemas of initial elements of Type.ARRAY.
variable_declarations.schema.prefix_item.rationale: Defines schemas for specific array positions. This validates input structure rather than security.

variable_declarations.schema.properties.rationale: Defines object properties within the schema. This describes expected input rather than enforcing security controls.

variable_declarations.schema.ref.description:
Allows indirect references between schema nodes. The value should be a
valid reference to a child of the root 'defs'.
For example, the following schema defines a reference to a schema node
named "Pet":
type: object
properties:
  pet:
    ref: #/defs/Pet
defs:
  Pet:
    type: object
    properties:
      name:
        type: string
The value of the "pet" property is a reference to the schema node
named "Pet".
See details in
https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/structuring.
variable_declarations.schema.ref.rationale: References another schema definition within the root defs structure.It organizes reusable schema components rather than defining a platform-level security control.

variable_declarations.schema.required.rationale: Specifies required object properties. While it validates input completeness, the required fields depend on the application's design rather than a generic security policy.

variable_declarations.schema.title.rationale: Provides a title for the schema. This is informational only.

variable_declarations.schema.type.description:
The type of the data.
Possible values:
STRING
INTEGER
NUMBER
BOOLEAN
OBJECT
ARRAY
variable_declarations.schema.type.rationale: Specifies the data type expected by the schema. This validates input but does not directly improve the application' security posture.

variable_declarations.schema.unique_item.description: Indicate the items in the array must be unique. Only applies to TYPE.ARRAY.
variable_declarations.schema.unique_item.rationale: Requires array items to be unique. This is a data validation feature rather than a generic security control.
